manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the bottle on the table and lift it.

Task description: The target is the white bottle with a light-purple cap on the table. Grasp and lift it off the table, keeping its cap facing upward.

Success criteria: The bottle is grasped and lifted with its base clear of the table and body nearly vertical, cap up and base down.

## Execution tips

- Try to grip a straight middle section below the bottle shoulder and above the base, with both pads contacting opposite sides. Avoid the cap and sloping shoulder to reduce slipping or rotation.
- Set the gripper opening slightly wider than the bottle body at the grasp point. During approach, keep the fingertips clear of the table to avoid scraping it or pushing the bottle over from one side.
- Before closing, use the head and right-side cameras to confirm the bottle body is actually between the fingers and that both pads have room to contact it. Do not mistake image overlap for enclosing the body.
- Lift slightly to check whether the bottle slides down or tilts, keeping its current upright pose where possible. If it needs to be grasped again, first let its base rest on the table before releasing.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start only this real-robot episode with the specified parameters, following the returned manual and live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode and report my observation-based assessment and the recording directory.

I have read the specified manual; only the right arm is available. The bottle is upright and the gripper is open. I am aligning with the bottle while maintaining clearance above the table, then will approach in small steps and check the positions of both pads.
The bottle remains upright and has not been touched. I adjusted the approach direction to align with its body; next I will continue approaching in small steps using both camera views.

During approach, the controller reported a recoverable singular-pose rejection after the arm moved partway. The bottle remains upright and ungrasped. I will adjust the pose using the returned measured position and try another reachable path within this episode.

Reachable movement resumed after pose adjustment. The bottle body is nearly centered in the right camera. I am continuing the approach in steps no larger than 1 cm, checking whether the bottle is being pushed or tilted.

The bottle’s position and orientation are currently stable. The wrist joint is approaching its limit during the approach, so I will continue adjusting pitch and height, confirm that the grasp area is around the middle of the bottle body, and then close the gripper.

The gripper remains open, and the bottle has not visibly moved. I am making the final lateral and depth adjustments; after confirming the bottle is enclosed, I will test-lift slightly to check grasp stability.

After closing, the measured opening is approximately 56 mm, and both pads appear to contact the bottle body. I will first lift 0.7 cm to check whether its bottom clears the table and whether it slips or tilts.

The bottle did not continuously rise with the gripper during the test lift, so a secure grasp cannot be confirmed. I will return to the original grasp height, confirm table support, then open, deepen enclosure and regrasp.

After increasing grasp depth, the opening is stable at about 59 mm, and the bottle showed signs of following the test lift. I will continue raising vertically in small steps, watching bottom clearance and bottle pose.

Live observations show that the bottle has risen with the gripper, nearly upright with its cap up. No obvious sliding was observed after holding still for 1.5 seconds. I will end this episode; the on-site operator will confirm whether it meets the success conditions for scene 003.
